“In the Garden of Eden Adam saw the animals before he named…” — Alfred North Whitehead (Q0274)

An English quotation associated with The Aims of Education, organized here under education.

Quotes / Alfred North Whitehead / Q0274

English

In the Garden of Eden Adam saw the animals before he named them: in the traditional system, children named the animals before they saw them.
Thinker Alfred North Whitehead
School Process Philosophy
Source The Aims of Education
Theme Education
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with The Aims of Education, within the Process Philosophy tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of education, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Alfred North Whitehead's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
